sentences.text: The holotype specimen of Leurospondylus ultimus was a juvenile animal.
The specific name ultimus means 'last' because the genus represented the latest known fossil plesiosaur at the time of its description.
The holotype was found in the brackish Edmonton beds of the present-day Red Deer River, which are part of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada.
The genus Leurospondylus was described by Brown in 1913.
The fossils were found in the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in Alberta, Canada, specifically within the brackish Edmonton beds of the present-day Red Deer River.
Samuel Paul Welles noted that the vertebrae resemble those of pliosaurs while the shoulder bones resemble those of elasmosaurids, making family classification difficult.
It is unknown whether Leurospondylus grew up and left the freshwater ecosystem or remained there as an adult.
The family of Leurospondylus is disputed, though it is suggested to belong to Elasmosauridae.
The Paleobi Database lists the parent group of Leurospondylus as Elasmosauridae.
Leurospondylus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Leurospondylus lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
It is debated whether the Leurospondylus specimen is a juvenile of a known species or belongs to an unrecognized taxonomic group.
